item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
• I’m suggesting you don’t use experiment logs at all, and just summarize the results in the description… 99% of experiment logs just seem like wasted word use, because we just wanna see the results anyway
  • I’m suggesting you cut the K-class event entirely, and come up with a less vague grandiose reason why the seer wants to work with the foundation. Genuinely find the tossing out of “it’s the end of the world” to be overused and distracting… especially when it’s not the focus of the article
  • and I think it’s good your focus will be on unpacking the anomaly… but then that leaves the question: what is the arc of the narrative? For example, what is the climax and resolution? What is the change in status quo from the beginning to the end of the article?

item.title: Re: First time SCP-Writer
item.content:encoded:
I’m concerned that this is overly generic. Right now you don’t seem like you have any plan for how you’re going to make the article interesting. You do mention “multiple anomalous effects” but you never elaborate on what they are.

If I may, I do have a few suggestions for ways to make this stand out. If you want to go for a more cute article, The Foundation could sport the latest in non lethal weaponry: fluff guns. If you’re looking for a comedic article you could have interns be reprimanded for trying to sneak into the cell and snuggle the rabbit. If you want to make it more worrying, I could see the area of effect on the fluff increasing. Slowly, the guards start trying to snuggle the rabbit and now we have a containment breach on our hands.

Whatever you decide to do, try to keep in mind that the article isn’t just about your anomaly. It’s about the story you’re telling. That story doesn’t have to be a 100 page novel with character arcs, but the reader should be learning about more than just your creature. Otherwise, why don’t they just read about one of the other beasts on the site?


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: First time SCP-Writer

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

So I appreciate all the work going into revising this, and for the most part you had me… and then I got to the end:

Sir Reginald's mental state improves, but the various other characters manifested from the SCP-A-2 event can't cope with the nature of their reality either, killing themselves. Sir Reginald enters a delusional state after his last friend dies, interacting with thin air as if his friends still existed. The article ends with a note from Sir Reginald, explaining that he tried everything, but he couldn't take it anymore, with Sir Reginald killing himself too in one moment of lucidity.

Can I suggest that him merely “losing his mind” and then wanting to kill himself is a weak way to explore someone’s difficulty in coming to terms with the fact that he used to he a fictional character? It’s just a bit tropey, and could be much more haunting if he’s just having to accept his lot over a slow process of accepting what’s happened…

Additionally, I think the introduction of the other fictional characters make a distracting element. Focus on on Reginald, and his grappling with this situation.

No one says this has to end in tragedy of such a dramatic nature… consider how sad it is for someone in his position to come to grips with his unreality, and now being fully aware, would be contained for the foreseeable future…

You could utilize psychoanalytic therapy sessions to explore his feelings on the matter and that would be a killer article. Therefore shifting away from the importance of the crazy circumstances and instead telling a grounded story of someone trying to understand who they are.

item.title: The Idol, seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and Tale

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout with a timeline of events addendum. Possible diary addendum for the tale.

Elevator Pitch: A little statue, that attracts people and creates a sense of purpose and community in people by altering their perception. Closeness to it gives peace and a general sense of wellbeing, distance causes a general sense of slight illness. Those feelings can be strong, but are perfectly manageable.

+ Central Narrative Hook and Notes
-collapse

Central Narrative: The core idea perhaps isn't too original, but I was more interested in how it would affects groups of people. How they would organize themselves if they all want to be as close as possible to the statue but at the same time know that in its presence they won't notice their hunger and tiredness and so they might kill themselves. Furthermore they know that they won't be allowed to keep the statue, there are those who will come to take it away, to contain it. So how they plan for it.
And I also try t explore a bit how people who are not exposed to the statue react to it. Sure, the organization tries to contain it, but there might be others who see it as an opportunity.
So beside the basic structure I would present a timeline of the events that led to the capture of the object, and a story in the first person about an attempt to steal it in order to expose a whole SCP facility.
I think presenting it as an addendum works better for one narrative, while presenting it as a story works better for a different narrative.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Rather than just the danger posed by the anomalous properties themselves I was interested in how the existence of those anomalous properties represent a thought hazard in those who know of them.

Additional Notes: I already wrote it and put it on my sandbox, mostly because I was interested in the idea and wanted to expand it, I would like some feedback and I would like to see if other people would enjoy it a much. It's mostly complete, but there are some things that can change based on feedback.
For instance in my original draft the timeline was more detailed and longer, then I streamlined it to the essentials, but I can expand it again if there's interest in it.

item.title: Re: The Laughing Tree
item.content:encoded:
So my biggest concern is this part:

Many of these children later runaway from home, but some of them return to the tree, carve their name in its trunk and kill themselves.

My concern is two-fold:
a) using suicide (especially of children!) as shock value in a skip is so grim dark edgy that I lose interest immediately… using suicide in a skip needs to be handled delicately, and earning that edgy subject matter with some of substance. Here it feels unearned
b) the thing what which makes you crazy, and/or kill yourself, is such an overwrought trope on the wiki that I just tend to lose interest. The thing making you crazy/kill yourself really has to say something interesting/new or it’ll just feel cliched. I don’t see much here to suggest you’re pushing through the usual tropes of using such a compulsion effect on an anomaly.

item.title: Re: Muy verdadero Re rate -1
item.content:encoded:
Muy verdadero 2, final.

I agree, the authors are free to write the hell they want but my point still remains, why?

I know it may sounds conspirational, but to be honest this reinterpretation doesn't add anything substantial to the table (for me), and I think that's my problem with this article.

I'm not sure what was the reasoning behind the rewrite. I share the concerns about the original article and I really wanted them to be changed but instead, we received a cervid like creature that in my humble opinion doesn't have any resemblance to the skip from the original article. (I know we got hints of the nature of her mother and the teenager in the previous iteration of the article)

I think that another thing that bothers me about rewrites (specially old articles) is that this kind of skips would never have as much upvotes as this one has right now. I don't even think this would be greenlighted (The Gaea) if a new writter tried to pull this thing off.

And that leaves wondering about two things

1.- As I said before, if the reinterpretation of the article was really to portray a more coherent or perhaps a more sensitive version of the succubus, why not changing the things that were disturbing? and perhaps construct the anomaly from there.

2.- I don't think this anomaly is better in any sense than the previous one, I think the original was not that particularly good, but it was series 1, so… hell, but this re interpretation doesn't feel as an improvement at all. I think it doesn't have any remarkable aspects that may better from it's previous iteration.

So… Why bother? Who asked for this? I think my issue here, is that this looks like as an article rewritten because it needed to be censored.

Well, that being said, this is an opinion though, take it as such, the author is always gonna be on the right in this kind of things.

For me this rewrite is a -1

btw: What happens with the people that upvoted this article for the succubus?

item.title: Re: The Unneeded Pact of Fire
item.content:encoded:
A woman (SCP-XXXX-01) leaves to get supplies for the town, and when returning notices the SCP Foundation has descended on the settlement. She sees the Foundation as the “bad guys”, and eventually makes a deal with SCP-XXXX to allegedly get rid of the Foundation in the area and save her town and family from the harsh winter. This ties her to SCP-XXXX, and she is now charged with keeping the fire lit and SCP-XXXX-02 at bay.

So my biggest problem is that, like Caspian above, I feel there's way too much unexplained here:

  • What is -2?
  • Why would the SCP Foundation be at the town when it sounds like the SCP wasn't active yet? (as there's no deal made until -1 sees the Foundation and then makes a pact with the Chiniea)
  • What the hell is the chininea that it can make such a deal? and how did the deal benefit anyone? And Why is -1 of the impression that Foundation is the enemy? What year did this take place?

I think you need to look at what you've put down here in the post and see what's missing from the post that you take for granted. Remember we're not in your head, so we need it laid out in the post itself. The article itself can be mysterious, but this post should be more transparent.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for new, wholesome-ish SCP
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for taking a look! Response below.

+ show block
– hide block

I have no specific narrative planned at the moment. What I have is just beats I wanted to hit and concepts to play with: the "Home Sweet Home" sign and the out-of-place doll suggests a potential story about someone without a home finding one in the doll house.

I imagine a D-Class or researcher who never really knew her/his/their family possessing the doll and not wanting to leave the house, the narrative borne out chiefly through radio communication logs (perhaps through a toy walkie-talkie placed in the house that then turns into a high-quality two-way radio from the subject possessing the doll's perspective) and/or journal entries. Perhaps the D-Class's description of the place and how nice it is makes a researcher jealous and they end up switching places with them without permission? Though I don't know how they'd think they'd get away with that for long…

Then maybe the research team purposely switches to a test subject that had a happier home life or whose psychological profile suggests they'd get bored or feel trapped. They reason that test subject would eventually want to leave and explore outside the house…

Perhaps, actually, it would be best to get rid of the possibility of switching out test subjects, and just have enough evidence discovered beforehand for them to know the best way to set up an experiment. The person that goes in is stuck there until they die walking through the portal. This could lay the narrative on a single character, and prevent the research team from simply changing test subjects before they get too comfortable inside…

Sorry, I guess this turned into more brainstorming than anything. I know I haven't given a lot of specifics, but does any of this feel like a step in the right direction or have I still not provided enough to work with? (I imagine the latter. Sorry if I'm wasting your time.)

item.title: Re: Laugh Track 1952
item.content:encoded:
Nit picks:

+ show block
– hide block
  • I don't want you to take this the wrong way, but there's not much to this idea. You don't even explain how the D-class are dying? they faint and then they wake up and they hear the laugh track over and over… So why does this lead to their deaths?
  • More importantly, why is the Foundation bothering to expose D-Class to the track twice a year? or however frequently it is?

Every once in a while, the laugh track (1-4) will go off, similar to that of a sitcom. This makes the subjects life a literal sitcom

This is just dropped into it, but this seems like the meat of the article as its major reshuffling of reality… then its not discussed at all beyond this.

  • Why are there 4 different laugh tracks? Do they do something different? If not, consider dropping the different versions.

Overall:
I feel like this is missing any sort of narrative. As it stands currently, it would be more fitting as an addition to the anomalous items list document… If you want to make this into its own article, I think you need to think about what more you want to say.

  • What are the stakes?
  • What is the overall arc?
  • How was this discovered?
  • What are the origins of the this anomaly?
  • Who could the reader relate to in the article?
  • What themes are you looking to explore?

item.title: SCP-XXXX: A Perfect Suburban Family
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: Completely normal family and Suburban house, or so it would seem. Somewhat self-containing, but regularly monitored. Strange sightings and initial anomalous properties such as extreme temperature.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation caught wind of the supposed SCP due to a 911 call. As Foundation Agents further investigate the home and family they give contradictory reports. Initial reports show evidence that the home and entities residing in it exhibit anomalous properties. Further reports however state that there is nothing anomalous, and the Agents themselves suddenly become increasingly adamant that everything is perfectly normal and dismiss their own initial evidence which proved otherwise. A field test is done and Agents participating in it conduct separate investigations. All initial investigations during the field test turn up similar evidence of anomalous behavior. Further investigations done by the same agents show no evidence of anomalous behavior, as well as the Agents confidently stating that everything is normal. Foundation scientists theorize the home and family may be connected somehow, maybe even being one single entity that tries to keep up its own veil of normality around it for unknown reasons. Initial investigations turn up evidence of an anomaly, but later investigations do not as the SCP "fixes" evidence of its anomalous properties so it doesn't show up again for individual investigators. Individuals investigating are also affected by this "fix." The anomalous effects most likely apply individually. This theory is accepted and the home and family are classified as SCP-XXXX. Anyone investigating or documenting the SCP must work on it only once, and immediately report their findings. All initial evidence has been shown individually and only once to O5-██, O5-██, and the Ethics Committee for confirmation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Is this a misunderstanding and the SCP Foundation is investigating a normal family, or is something else going on here?

Additional Notes:

The SCP procedure of "only work on it once" gets implemented later for the documentation part, due to changes to the SCP document made by affected individuals (possible gimmick I'm thinking about) Furthermore, in the article itself it won't be as obvious that the home and family really are an SCP.

I'm mainly looking for constructive criticism. I'm basically just throwing the idea out there which is why it's plain and basic at this stage, and somewhat confusing.

Forum thread: SCP-XXXX: A Perfect Suburban Family

item.title: Re: Transfer consciousness to a non-physical entity
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Helghastt. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I was following the concept decently enough till it got to the anomalous part. Okay, so it’s a sleeping pod, yes? When someone gets in, a gas forces them to sleep. And then what? What exactly is SCP-xxxx-1? What exactly is this “non-physical entity right next to SCP-XXXX”?

I think the physical mechanics of the object are sound. I like your inclusion of historical background as a potential discovery log, as with the potential for the scp to be tested in the field by the Foundation. But I’m having trouble actually picturing the object.

Apart from that, my other main concern is that it’s just not very interesting. I’m sorry to be blunt, but it’s basically an incorporeal capsule that can transport people around? There isn’t much intrigue, tension or conflict present in the concept. One way you can try fixing this is adding some element of danger to the scp. So it can transport people around, but use it too often / too long, and there will be detrimental effects, for example.

More work has to be done here to get to greenlight status. If you decide to revise your concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: SCP: The Crusader Pond
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Undead Jastus. Let’s take a look at your concept.

Okay, so the premise is intriguing: basically a religious site that compels visitors to act in a certain way. I’m still not too sure about how the various parts of the concept fit together though. Perhaps you can explain the following:

1) How does a pond link to the Templar Knights? Essentially, what’s the significance of this location to this historical group?
2) Who is making these visitors become violent? If you’re using the Templars, is there a greater entity (i.e. God or a deceased Knight) who is pulling the strings?
3) How does the faith of the Knights Templar equals violence towards the SCP. This link isn’t clear. You say that the SCP (for example) would be considered “against their faith”. Why?

item.title: Re: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
1) You did fine on the waves. I hate saying it's all pseudo-science anyway and we expect some hand-waving, but you did fine.

2) This is a pretty good SCP. You have the basic something that has to come from somewhere trope, and it feels pretty good here instead of cliched. In that regard, kudos.

3) If you end up writing it up, try to avoid the idol issue: The girl becomes more popular the sadder she gets. While it makes sense, especially as she makes people feel better so it's only natural that she draws people in, you want to keep it where it's at, where the others become more interested in their happiness and ignore the cause of it.

4) If you want to up the drama, put the webcam on a tripod at the end so we see her falling into the river. Not only does it provide certainty of her fate, but it also makes a great capstone to the tale. You may also want to mention to whom she's giving the pom-poms just to keep the terror going. However, keep in mind that The Foundation has to grab them at some point, so you need to keep in mind that there has to be some way for them to get involved.

Otherwise, great idea and follow-through!

item.title: Re: Humanity, for Dummies
item.content:encoded:
While I like the idea in general, the problem is there is no actual SCP at the heart of it. You've ironically switched the usual problem: While most submissions have a great SCP with no narrative, you have a great narrative with no SPC. You need to back this with an interesting SCP as well.

However, your narrative does have two flaws: First, in demanding the papers the SCP now has to choose between the worth of the information versus the worth of the lives in question. If the information has any worth then it may be worth sacrificing those in danger to keep the information safe, especially if it involves operating information or a dangerous SCP. You may want to remove that plot line.

Second, you may want to start with a sympathetic SCP in the first place. Not all humanoid SCPs are vicious monsters; in fact, most of them are victims themselves. Also, it becomes a lot harder for the concept if you need to create sympathy in a hardened SCP; it's just better to start with one that's a better foil for The Foundation's issues to begin with, both for symbolism and plot purposes. A scared kid or guy that's been forced to attack works far better than an SCP that was caught doing what it does.

This is a great idea, it just has some issues. Good luck!

item.title: Corpse of a Dead God
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, History

Page Layout: Containment procedure, description, tests, interview, personal report, final addendum.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a mummified body with a human torso, arms, and head, but it has animalistic legs, a tail, and horns. The mouth and eyelids are closed. It is completely unresponsive to people and could be easily written off as being dead. It has been reported to been speaking Doric Greek, Latin, and a third unknown language. It will never move and is quiet limp, but the body itself will never wither or fall apart, remaining perfectly intact. Flora will emerge in the surrounding area and will continue to grow, and if a dissection is attempted its mouth will snap open and a loud, ear-bleeding scream will emerge from it for a small period of time.

Central Narrative: (From a diary) The body was discovered in a hidden grotto on the island of Paxi in the 1950s. It was bought by the Brazilian ceo of a food processing company. who had a fascination with occult symbols and strange artifacts. The body was accidentally delivered to his hotel room near a deforested site. The next day, the sight was completely regrown. After some more "experiments" he concluded that this body could restore the earth's lost flora and fauna. But instead of using it as a way to fix deforestation, he used it to essentially create infinite resources for his own profit. He saw nothing wrong with this, claiming that if the body didn't want him to prosper, it would regrow the wild. It came as no surprise by his blue collar workers (he thought he was a witch) when he and the body disappeared, and soon his colleagues and some workers.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I don't believe there's any SCP quiet like this. It's a mummified corpse that's really a powerful being trapped in pathetically useless body but can still use all of its powers is a literary contradiction but a narratively important one. It explores an interesting side of big business, about how often times they try to mask their destructive actions against nature with claims of the corporation being safe and loving nature and whatnot.

Additional Notes: Of course I'll expand on it much more on my draft.

item.title: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a pair of Pom Poms each having identical red, white, and blue stripes they don't display any signs of considerable wear. When a human holds SCP-XXXX, hereafter designed SCP-XXXX-1, will have their memories erased that caused them strong euphoria, this process can take only a few minutes or hours depending on the number of memories. When SCP-XXXX-1 has no more memories that can be extracted they will start to emit waves, when these waves contact a human will cause an immediate euphoria, the amount of euphoria, the length of the waves, and how long they experience euphoria is dependent on how many memories were erased to SCP-XXXX-1.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this piece would take the form of the recordings of a Webcam taking place in a high school with two sisters named Lyvia, and Emily. All recordings were made by Lyvia until the last recording. The first recording shows the discovery of SCP-XXXX when they join a cheerleading club. Over time the recordings show the increasing depression of Emily.Almost all of the recordings show the parents of Emily and Lyvia being filled with happiness ignoring the well-being of Emily this resulted in Emily isolating herself to a nearby lake. The last recording shows Emily facing a lake repeating these questions: Who are they? Where am I? Why can't I feel anything? Why is everybody so happy?. This recording lasts until a faint sound of a splash due to the webcam being water damaged though the memory chip was unaffected.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The primary hook of this article is the way it shows how it affects SCP-XXXX-1, and the people near them. As people read the recordings they will feel more attached once it shows the connection between Emily with her family. The Pom Poms are based on a simple concept(Pom Poms that make you sadder, and make people near you happier)but gets more tragic when it goes more in-depth on its discovery.

Additional Notes: If somebody could show me a better way to explain the happy waves that would be splendid!

The goldfish was found when a shopkeeper of a fishstore heard voices from an aquarium which he reported to the police, then the Foundation heard about this and visited the fish store, there, a field agent found a goldfish that staring at her, the agent tapped the glass of the aquarium, enough to scare the other goldfish, but this goldfish didn't faze at all, and let out an annoyed voice saying that it was angry that she tapped the aquarium too hard with a venom on its voice. The Foundation later on transfered the goldfish to the Foundation and they fabricated the report from the shopkeeper, the shopkeeper however received a class B amnestics.

The goldfish is contain in a 3x3 cell room, inside the cell room is a 400 gallon rectangular aquarium, with 96"Lengthx36"Widthx36xHeight with aquarium necessity(like water filter etc) to keep the aquarium clean, comfortable and fresh, so that the goldfish can't teleport from unclean aquarium because it was uncomfortable and hated the water quality.

The goldfish can escape since nothing can stop it from teleporting from water source to water source, but only when its aquarium is unclean. For now, it won't want to escape.
